memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The king of Sodom said to Abram, "Give me the people and keep the goods for yourself." But Abram said to the king of Sodom, "With raised hand I have sworn an oath to the Lord, God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth, that I will accept nothing belonging to you, not even a thread or the strap of a sandal, so that you will never be able to say, 'I made Abram rich.'" - Gen 14:21-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Now the second king makes his offer, and it is generous: "keep the goods for yourself." Abram had every legal right to the spoils of war. This was his by the custom of the day, earned by risk and courage. And he refuses. Not a thread. Not a sandal strap.

Why such a strong refusal? Abram tells us: "so that you will never be able to say, 'I made Abram rich.'" He would not let Sodom claim credit for what God had promised to provide. God had said, "I will bless you" (Gen 12:2), and Abram would not muddy that promise by taking a handout from a corrupt king.

Notice the contrast with chapter 12. There, Abram had taken wealth from a pagan king - Pharaoh - through deceit and fear, and it went badly. He has learned. Failure taught him something, and now he refuses what he once grabbed. God's people can grow.

There is real freedom in Abram's refusal. He was free to walk away from money because his security rested elsewhere. Paul knew the same freedom: "I have learned to be content whatever the circumstances" (Phil 4:11). Some blessings cost too much. When the world offers you something that would let it claim credit for your life, you can afford to say no.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Is there an offer you should refuse because of who could claim credit for you?
- Has a past failure taught you something you're now living differently?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You are the One who provides for me. Give me the freedom to refuse what would let the world claim credit for Your goodness. Let my life declare that You alone are my portion.
Amen.
